activities.title: Establish the context register with climate relevance review
activities.description: Maintain the organizational context register and include a deliberate review of whether climate change is relevant to the QMS context.
activities.objective: Create a reasoned, current context decision that records climate relevance when it can affect QMS outcomes.
activities.why_it_matters: A visible relevance decision helps the organization focus planning on conditions that can affect customers, processes, resources, supply continuity, or intended results without assuming that every organization has a climate-related QMS risk.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Gather internal and external context inputs as in the initial method.
2. Consider whether climate change is relevant to the QMS context.
3. Record RELEVANT or NOT CURRENTLY RELEVANT with a concise rationale.
4. If relevant, describe material implications and connect them to planning or action records.
5. Set periodic and change-triggered review points.
activities.expected_output: An approved context register containing a climate relevance decision, rationale, implications where relevant, ownership, and review triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include the maintained context register, climate relevance decision, rationale, implication notes, review record, and follow-up actions where material.
activities.success_criteria: Context inputs are current, the climate relevance decision is explicit and reasoned, material implications are linked to suitable planning, and both periodic and change-triggered reviews are defined.

activities.title: Evaluate interested-party inputs including climate relevance
activities.description: Maintain the interested-party register with a clear distinction between an input being expressed and that input being relevant to QMS planning.
activities.objective: Give the organization a repeatable way to evaluate climate-related and other interested-party inputs without treating every request as a QMS obligation.
activities.why_it_matters: Separate relevance decisions keep stakeholder listening useful and proportionate while making material changes visible to QMS owners.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Capture the need, expectation, constraint, or information being expressed.
2. Identify the source and context of the input.
3. Decide whether the input is relevant to the QMS and record the rationale.
4. Assign monitoring ownership and a review trigger.
5. Include climate-related inputs where they are actually relevant and link material effects to QMS actions.
activities.expected_output: A reviewed interested-party register with input descriptions, relevance decisions, rationales, monitoring owners, and review triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a relevant-party register, captured input, relevance decision, rationale, monitoring assignment, review record, and linked planning action where needed.
activities.success_criteria: Inputs are distinguished from relevance decisions, climate-related inputs are considered where appropriate, owners and review triggers are clear, and relevant changes can reach QMS planning.

activities.title: Plan QMS risks, opportunities, and significant changes
activities.description: Connect context and interested-party inputs to proportionate risk or opportunity decisions and add a pre-implementation planning route for significant QMS changes.
activities.objective: Make significant QMS changes understandable and planned before implementation while keeping risk and opportunity judgement proportionate.
activities.why_it_matters: Early change planning protects QMS continuity and integrity by making purpose, consequences, resources, responsibility, implementation route, and follow-up visible before execution.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Review context and interested-party inputs for QMS implications.
2. Decide whether a risk, opportunity, or no further risk treatment is appropriate.
3. For a significant planned QMS change, record its purpose and potential consequences.
4. Plan continuity, integrity, resources, responsibilities, authorities, and implementation route.
5. Define follow-up and effectiveness review.
6. Connect resource, operational-change, and leadership actions where the plan requires them.
activities.expected_output: A maintained risk and opportunity register plus a proportionate pre-implementation QMS change plan for significant changes.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include context links, risk or opportunity decisions, change purpose, consequence review, resource and responsibility decisions, implementation route, and follow-up record.
activities.success_criteria: Relevant inputs inform judgement, significant changes are planned before implementation, continuity and resources are addressed, owners are clear, and follow-up is defined without converting every context item into a risk.
activities.responsible_role: Quality Manager with Leadership and Process Owners

activities.title: Plan QMS resources and organizational knowledge
activities.description: Plan QMS resources while making the organizational knowledge needed to operate key processes visible and reviewable.
activities.objective: Connect resource decisions with available knowledge, retention, transfer, and changing knowledge needs.
activities.why_it_matters: Important know-how can be lost or unavailable at the point of need even when headcount and equipment appear adequate. A proportionate knowledge view helps the organization protect reliable process performance.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify knowledge needed for key processes and QMS priorities.
2. Review what knowledge is available and where it is needed.
3. Identify retention, sharing, transfer, single-person dependency, or knowledge-loss exposure.
4. Record changing or externally acquired knowledge needs.
5. Assign proportionate resource actions, owners, timing, and review triggers.
activities.expected_output: A prioritized QMS resource and organizational-knowledge plan with availability, retention, transfer, and changing-needs decisions.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include resource assessment, process knowledge needs, availability review, retention or transfer action, dependency review, and follow-up decisions.
activities.success_criteria: Resource needs and knowledge needs are connected, material gaps are visible, knowledge is available at the point of need, and actions remain proportionate to the organization.
activities.responsible_role: Top Management with Quality Manager and Process Owners

activities.title: Establish competence and organizational knowledge decisions
activities.description: Define competence requirements and keep the distinct organizational knowledge needed to operate processes visible in related decisions.
activities.objective: Connect person capability decisions with knowledge retention and transfer without treating training records or a competence matrix as complete knowledge management.
activities.why_it_matters: A person can attend training without demonstrating capability, and an organization can hold important know-how outside any one person's competence record. The distinction supports better action selection.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Define the capability needed for quality-impacting work.
2. Review evidence of competence through experience, qualification, coaching, supervised practice, or observed performance.
3. Identify organizational knowledge needed beyond an individual person's capability.
4. Plan proportionate knowledge capture, retention, transfer, access, or external acquisition where relevant.
5. Check action effectiveness and reassess after material changes.
activities.expected_output: Competence requirements with owned actions and a connected record of material organizational-knowledge retention or transfer needs.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include competence requirements, capability review, qualification or practice evidence, knowledge-retention action, transfer record, and effectiveness follow-up.
activities.success_criteria: Competence is evaluated as person capability, organizational knowledge is treated as a distinct need, actions address both where relevant, and effectiveness is reviewed.

activities.title: Control operational changes after QMS change planning
activities.description: Control operational changes when they reach execution, while preserving the separate pre-implementation QMS change-planning route.
activities.objective: Make operational change impact, authorization, communication, verification, controlled-information updates, and follow-up visible in execution.
activities.why_it_matters: Operational execution needs a practical control point that carries a planned change into the work without collapsing all QMS change planning into an operational checklist.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Describe the operational change and its relationship to any approved QMS change plan.
2. Assess operational impact and required authorization.
3. Communicate the change to affected people and providers.
4. Complete verification or validation where relevant before normal use.
5. Update controlled information and record the execution decision.
6. Perform a post-change review when impact or risk warrants follow-up.
activities.expected_output: A proportionate operational-change record showing impact, authorization, communication, execution controls, and follow-up.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include change description, impact assessment, authorization, communication, verification result, controlled-information update, and post-change review.
activities.success_criteria: Operational changes are authorized and understood, needed verification and information updates occur, affected parties are informed, and follow-up is proportionate.

activities.title: Prepare management review inputs for significant QMS changes
activities.description: Include significant QMS changes and relevant climate or interested-party developments in normal management review inputs when material.
activities.objective: Turn meaningful QMS change information into leadership decisions, resources, ownership, timing, and follow-up.
activities.why_it_matters: Leadership review is more useful when significant changes are evaluated with performance information and result in owned decisions instead of being treated as a separate meeting.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Gather significant QMS change plans, execution results, context changes, interested-party inputs, and performance information where material.
2. Present implications and open decisions to leadership.
3. Record the leadership decision, owner, resource need, timing, and follow-up expectation.
4. Link decisions to QMS actions and review their status.
5. Adjust review inputs when decisions show that information is incomplete or not useful.
activities.expected_output: Management review inputs and decisions that capture significant QMS changes, owners, resources, timing, and follow-up where relevant.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include change input summary, leadership decision, assigned owner, resource action, timing, linked action record, and follow-up review.
activities.success_criteria: Material QMS changes reach normal leadership review, decisions have ownership and timing, resource needs are visible, and follow-up is retained without creating a separate mandatory climate meeting.
